title: Rook vs pawn
tagline: The race where your king is the stopwatch

principles.prompt: Rook against a far-advanced pawn with king support. What decides the game?
principles.answer: Your own king's distance. Close enough to join the attack: win. Too far: the rook alone can only trade itself for the pawn — draw.

principles.prompt: Pawn on its 7th, enemy king beside it, your king one file away. Name the winning pattern.
principles.answer: Check from the side to force his king in front of the pawn, post your king on the adjacent file — and promotion runs into a back-rank mate.

principles.prompt: Why does the fresh queen sometimes die the move it's born?
principles.answer: In the corner she stands behind her own king: a rook check along the back rank can't be captured (the king blocks the queen's path) and can't be blocked. Mate.

principles.prompt: Your king is too far to help the rook. What can the rook still guarantee?
principles.answer: The draw: harass from behind and the side — the enemy king can shield the pawn or escort it forward, never both — and give the rook for the pawn at the last moment.

demos.title: Too far to win, close enough to draw
demos.intro: White's king is on another continent. Watch what the rook can — and can't — do alone.

steps.note: Drive the king in front of its pawn.
Into the corner — and note the trap: the pawn is now stuck behind its own king.
Careful! Keeping the b-file pinned would be stalemate. Step aside and wait.
Out again, ready to step off and promote…
…and straight back in front. This is the whole story:
This time the king steps away from the pawn —
— and the rook instantly hits it from behind.
So the king returns, and the dance repeats forever. Shield or escort, never both: draw. Bring the white king two files closer and this same position is a win — that's the test.

tests.title: The promotion trap
tests.intro: Same pawn, but your king made it to c4 — close enough to spring the trap.

wrong.Rb3+: Kc2! slips around the rook and nothing stops a1=Q. Check along the rank — it pins his king to the pawn's fate.
wrong.Ra3: Kxa3 — the rook was undefended. Check first, approach second.
wrong.Kb4: a1=Q arrives — you had exactly one tempo and spent it on a quiet move.

hints: Force his king onto the promotion path first, then bring your own king to b3.
Rg2+, and after Kb1, Kb3! — now a1=Q walks into Rg1 mate: the queen is trapped behind her own king.

tests.explanationAfter: The full pattern: the rank check forced his king in front of the pawn, Kb3 took the guard post, and the brand-new queen on a1 couldn't stop Rg1# — her own king blocks every escape and the capture alike. King close: win.

tests.title: Trap at the top
tests.intro: White's h-pawn is one step from a new queen — and your king made it to f5 in time.

wrong.Rg6+: Kf7! and the pawn queens anyway — the file check let his king slip out sideways. Check along the rank instead.
wrong.Rh6: Kxh6 — the rook was undefended. Check first, approach second.
wrong.Ke6: h8=Q comes — the pawn was one move from glory and you looked away.

hints: Mirror of the last drill: rank check, then your king to g6.
Rb7+, Kg8 forced, then Kg6! — h8=Q is answered by Rb8 mate.

tests.explanationAfter: Same trap upside down: the rank check put his king on g8, Kg6 sealed the flight squares, and the newborn queen on h8 watched Rb8# arrive — blocked from capturing by her own king. Learn it once, use it from either side.
